messages.text: What's gone so wrong so quickly at Crystal Palace?

metadata.summary: As Pierre Sage waited to receive the Coupe de France trophy as the victorious manager of RC Lens last May, he turned to his staff and said: "Do you realise where we are?"
metadata.content: Pierre Sage under pressure: How Crystal Palace and last season's Ligue 1 manager of the year are both suffering | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Pierre Sage under pressure: How Crystal Palace and last season's Ligue 1 manager of the year are both suffering Pierre Sage struggling for results at Selhurst Park after loss of Daniel Munoz and Maxence Lacroix plus injury to Ismaila Sarr - but bigger questions remain; watch Crystal Palace vs Liverpool live on Sky Sports Main Event from 12.30pm on Sunday, kick-off 2pm Ron Walker Football Journalist @Ronnabe Sunday 8 November 2026 13:56, UK As Pierre Sage waited to receive the Coupe de France trophy as the victorious manager of RC Lens last May, he turned to his staff and said: "Do you realise where we are?" Sage had just led the club to a first French Cup title in its history while plotting a course to finish second in Ligue 1, its joint-best league position in over two decades - all in his first season in charge. Having managed only 56 professional games prior to joining the club, he had become the rising star of French football almost overnight. Less than six months on, the 47-year-old may be glad he took that moment to embrace the good times. messages.text: Liverpool's unwanted record highlights creativity issue

metadata.summary: Liverpool set an unwanted record against Arsenal as they failed to register a shot on target for the first time in 442 Premier League home games, dating back to when records began in 2003.
metadata.content: Liverpool's unwanted record against Arsenal shows creativity problem under Andoni Iraola - Between the Lines | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Liverpool's unwanted record against Arsenal shows creativity problem under Andoni Iraola - Between the Lines Liverpool failed to hit the target with 17 shots against Arsenal but creativity is a bigger issue than finishing; Between the Lines , the Sky Sports data strand, explains how Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz are contributing to the problem By Nick Wright and Adam Smith Sunday 8 November 2026 13:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We reveal the statistics behind Liverpool's creativity problem Liverpool set an unwanted record against Arsenal as they failed to register a shot on target for the first time in 442 Premier League home games, dating back to when records began in 2003. The ignominious statistic was confirmed by Opta, who initially credited Ronald Araujo and Alexis Mac Allister with shots on target but later ruled them as a blocked shot and overhit pass. Liverpool's finishing was wayward. They were also incorrectly denied a penalty. But a lack of creativity was the bigger issue. Their 17 shots were worth a meagre 1.05 expected goals. It was just the latest example of them struggling to create high-quality chances. messages.text: Russo shines at Anfield, United snatch late win - WSL round-up

metadata.summary: Arsenal claimed a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Liverpool at Anfield as Alessia Russo's double secured three important points for Renee Slegers' side, while Manchester United left it late to beat Aston Villa 1-0.
metadata.content: WSL: Liverpool 1-2 Arsenal, Aston Villa 0-1 Man Utd – Alessia Russo double inspires Gunners as Julia Zigiotti Olme earns late United win | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WSL: Liverpool 1-2 Arsenal, Aston Villa 0-1 Man Utd – Alessia Russo double inspires Gunners as Julia Zigiotti Olme earns late United win WSL round-up as Arsenal beat Liverpool 2-1 thanks to an Alessia Russo double, while Manchester United left it late to claim a 1-0 victory at Aston Villa, with Julia Zigiotti Olme scoring the decisive goal in the second half. By Sam Cohen Sunday 8 November 2026 15:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's Super League match between Liverpool and Arsenal. Arsenal claimed a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Liverpool at Anfield as Alessia Russo's double secured three important points for Renee Slegers' side, while Manchester United left it late to beat Aston Villa 1-0. Russo was the difference for Arsenal, opening the scoring after just eight minutes with a composed finish after being picked out by Emily Fox . Liverpool hit back seven minutes later through Beata Olsson , who got away from Leah Williamson before finding the net to bring the hosts level. But Russo had the final say before the break, arriving at the back post to head home Lisa Baum's delivery and restore Arsenal's lead. messages.text: English hopes fade as Pelaez hits hole-in-one en route to title in China

metadata.summary: England's Mimi Rhodes, Charlotte Heath and Annabell Fuller saw their hopes fade on the last day of the Aramco China Championship as Spain's Ana Pelaez stormed to her second Ladies European Tour title with a nine-under round that included a hole-in-one.
metadata.content: Aramco China Championship: Mimi Rhodes and fellow English players miss out on title as Spain's Ana Pelaez storms to victory | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Aramco China Championship: Mimi Rhodes and fellow English players miss out on title as Spain's Ana Pelaez storms to victory Spain's Ana Pelaez records seven birdies and a hole-in-one as she wins Ladies European Tour title in Shenzhen; England's Mimi Rhodes finishes outright second, three shots adrift, with compatriots Charlotte Heath and Annabell Fuller sealing top-10 places; Shuri Sakuma triumphs on LPGA Tour Sunday 8 November 2026 12:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of the Aramco China Championship as Spain's Ana Pelaez stormed to victory England's Mimi Rhodes, Charlotte Heath and Annabell Fuller saw their hopes fade on the last day of the Aramco China Championship as Spain's Ana Pelaez stormed to her second Ladies European Tour title with a nine-under round that included a hole-in-one. Heath shared the lead with Pelaez's compatriot Luna Sobron on 16 under after round three in Shenzhen, with Rhodes one shot back and Fuller three strokes adrift. Fuller stared superbly on Sunday with four birdies in her first six holes lifting her to 16 under but she then registered three bogeys on her back nine ahead of a closing birdie to end up on 14 under and in ninth spot after a one-under day, six shots behind Pelaez.
